handback.title: One settings file per repo over shipped defaults
handback.summary: Each repo sets only what differs from Dokima's shipped defaults, in one settings file.
handback.feature: A repo changes Dokima's behavior through one settings file. The first story builds the reader and workflows; the rest move code to settings.

stories.context: New `dokima/settings.py` reads `dokima/defaults.yaml` and `.dokima/settings.yaml` with PyYAML (owner allowed it). Today `dokima/setup.py` `read_settings()` reads only nested maps and `write_settings()` rewrites the file; `dokima/agents.py` reads `.dokima/agents.yml`. Workflow rows of the owner's list (A13 to A19, B3, B5, C3, C4, E1, E2, E4, E8, E11, E15) live in `.github/workflows/agent.yml`, `full-suite.yml`, `acceptance-criteria.yml`, `testmon.yml`, `fix.yml`, `wiki.yml`; the co-author trailer sits at `agent.yml:408` and `wiki.yml:27`. Locked keys: app-only identity, keys only from main, fence, judge runs main's copy, owner approval by default. The owner's newer comment makes the fence's test setup files a setting (row A5); newer words win, so the fence's lock covers what it does, not that list.

raises.label: Settle: file name
raises.text: Should a repo's settings file end in .yaml or .yml? The plan assumes .yaml, like the defaults file.
raises.evidence: The issue asks to settle `.yml` vs `.yaml` before building.

raises.label: Doubt: already fixed
raises.text: Two absorbed bugs look fixed already. The plan only pins each with a criterion. Is that right?

raises.label: Doubt: overlaps open issues
raises.text: Install command, exclude list and house rules are also asked in #744 and #741. Build here? The plan assumes so.
raises.evidence: #744 runs `tests.install` and `tests.exclude`; #741 adds `prompts.append`; your list rows A13 and E15.

answers.why: The scan now looks for every shipped default value, as its own last story.
Your list names each workflow value; each now has a criterion that reads it.
Named broken YAML, which fails naming the file, and both files, where the settings file wins.
